# Role Domains Reference

Complete reference for the `glassfrog domains` and `glassfrog domain` commands — the areas of control a role holds, read either as a role's list or one domain by its own id.

## Overview

Domains are exposed as **two sibling commands**, not children of `roles`:

- `glassfrog domains <ROLE_ID>` **lists** the domains a role controls (`GET /roles/{id}/domains`). Paginated — walks every page by default.
- `glassfrog domain <DOMAIN_ID>` **reads one domain** by its own id (`GET /domains/{id}`), optionally embedding its policies. Not paginated.

The two key off **different id types** (`role_…` for the list, `dom_…` for the single read), so each takes exactly one required positional. This is the addressable counterpart to the domains embedded inline on a role (`glassfrog roles <id>`) or a tree node (`glassfrog tree`).

Codebase enrichment skipped — not attempted. This reference is based on the interface contracts and the shipped `--help`.

## `glassfrog domains <ROLE_ID>` — list a role's domains

### Synopsis

```
glassfrog domains <ROLE_ID> [--query TERM] [--first-page] [--per-page N] [--base-url URL] [-o FORMAT]
```

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ROLE_ID` | string | required | The role whose domains are listed (`role_…`). Not validated locally; the API resolves it (an unknown/malformed id → `404`). |

### List flags

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--query`, `-q` | string | — | Full-text search over the role's domains (the API `q` parameter; Postgres FTS, Google-style syntax: `marketing -intern`, `"exact phrase"`, `foo OR bar`). Sent **only when the trimmed value is non-blank** — a blank/whitespace term is treated as no search. Composes with the walk (carried on every page). A malformed query returns an empty list, not an error. |
| `--first-page` | bool | false | Fetch only the first page and signal if more exist (see [Completeness signalling](#completeness-signalling)). |
| `--per-page` | int | API max | Page size for the walk. The API owns the valid range. |

`--include` is **rejected** on `domains` (related-resource embedding is a single-read concern) — a usage error, no request sent.

### List output

Rendered in the resolved format (see [Output formats](#output-formats)). Every format fetches the same domains; the format changes rendering, not fetch depth. By default the list walks to completion; `--first-page` limits all formats to one page.

**`full`** — one block per domain, blocks separated by a blank line; the description is the headline, the id trailing:

```
<domain description> (dom_0123…)
```

**`compact`** — one line per domain, id first then the description:

```
dom_0123…  <domain description>
```

**`json` / `yaml`** — the aggregated document `{ "data": [ <domain>, … ] }`, each domain's bytes preserved verbatim across the walk. Only the `data` envelope is synthesized; per-page `meta` is dropped.

**Empty result** (the role controls no domains, or `--query` matched none): under `full`/`compact`, stdout is exactly `No domains.` and the command exits `0`. Structured formats emit `{"data": []}` (never `null`).

## `glassfrog domain <DOMAIN_ID>` — single read

### Synopsis

```
glassfrog domain <DOMAIN_ID> [--include policies] [--base-url URL] [-o FORMAT]
```

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DOMAIN_ID` | string | required | The domain to read (`dom_…`). Not validated locally; the API resolves it (unknown → `404`). |

### Single-read flag

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--include` | string (comma-separated) | — | Related resources to embed (`?include=`). The only valid value is `policies`. Validated locally before any request; an unsupported value is a fail-fast usage error (the API would otherwise silently ignore it). |

`--query`/`--first-page`/`--per-page` are **rejected** on `domain` — the single read is unpaginated and unsearchable. They are declared only to return a helpful "use `domains <role-id>` instead" usage error (exit `2`, no request).

### Single-read output

**`full`** — the domain's description, id, and controlling role; when `--include policies` is requested, a guarded `Policies:` section (omitted when not requested):

```
<domain description> (dom_0123…)
  Role: <role_id | (no controlling role)>
  Policies:
    - <policy title>
    (none)
```

`Domain.role_id` is **nullable**: when it is null the render shows the explicit-absence marker `(no controlling role)`, never a fabricated or empty id. The `Policies:` section shows a standalone indented `(none)` line when requested but empty.

**`compact`** — one line:

```
dom_0123…  <domain description>  role=<role_id | (no controlling role)>
```

The policies embed is a `full`-only elaboration; `compact` stays one line.

**`json` / `yaml`** — the API's `{data: Domain}` body verbatim: no field dropped, no number coerced.

## Projection fields

### Domain (list and single)

| Field | Notes |
|---|---|
| Description | The domain's description; rendered as the headline with the id, e.g. `<description> (dom_0123…)`. |
| Role | The controlling role's id; `(no controlling role)` when `role_id` is null. |
| Policies | Present in the single read only, under `--include policies`; `(none)` when empty. |

## Completeness signalling

Applies to `domains` (the list). A partial list is never silently presented as complete — completeness is signalled via a note on **stderr**, never an in-band `meta`.

| Situation | Behaviour | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| Default (full walk) | Walks every page and renders the complete set. | 0 |
| `--first-page`, more pages exist | Renders the first page; writes to stderr: `note: more domains exist than shown; re-run without --first-page to fetch all` | 0 |
| Mid-walk failure | Renders domains gathered so far; writes to stderr: `note: result is incomplete — <cause>; the domains shown are a partial set` | non-zero |

The single `domain` read issues exactly one request — no walk, no completeness note.

## Output formats

Inherited persistent root flags, read by cobra inheritance:

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--base-url URL` | Override the API base URL (top rung of the base-URL precedence chain). |
| `-o`, `--output FORMAT` | `full` (default), `compact`, `json`, or `yaml` — or, at the flag only, a user-template ref (a template file path, or `stdin`; see [User-Defined Template Output](user-defined-template-output.md)). Resolution chain: flag → `GLASSFROG_OUTPUT` → `.glassfrogrc output` → `full` (env/config accept only the four tokens). |

The raw API envelope is never emitted under a human format (`full`/`compact`).

## Exit codes and errors

Failure rendering is **format-aware** (Output-Aware Failure Rendering): under `json`/`yaml` a failure emits the unified error envelope on **stdout** (so an agent parses success and failure the same way); under `full`/`compact` the diagnostic goes to **stderr**. The incompleteness note stays on **stderr** in every format. The exit code is the category from the Exit-Code Convention. Every diagnostic names the cause and a next step, and never includes the token.

| Condition | Exit | Diagnostic |
|---|---|---|
| Domains listed / domain read (incl. empty list, no-match search) | 0 | — (result on stdout; incompleteness note on stderr when applicable) |
| No usable token | 2 | "not authenticated — run `glassfrog auth login` or set GLASSFROG_TOKEN" |
| Unreadable / malformed credential file | 1 | names the path — "fix or remove the malformed `.glassfrogrc`" |
| Unknown/forbidden role or domain id, or other non-2xx (4xx/5xx) | 3 / 4 / 5 | names the HTTP status + extracted detail; per-class next step (permission: "check the token's access"; rate-limit: "retry later") |
| Could not reach the wire | 6 | names the transport failure + host — "check network access and the base URL" |
| 2xx body did not match the expected shape | 3 | "the API response did not match the expected shape — may be an API change; report it" |
| Malformed paging mid-walk (`domains`) | 1 | "the API returned malformed pagination — partial set shown" |
| Base-URL configuration error | 2 | names the malformed base URL + source |
| Invalid `--output` selector | 2 | names the bad format value + the four valid names |
| Unsupported `--include` value (`domain`) | 2 | names the unsupported value + the supported set `{policies}`; no request sent |
| `--include` on `domains`, a list flag on `domain`, or wrong positional count | 2 | names the misuse (e.g. "--include applies to the single `domain` read; use `glassfrog domain <id> --include policies`") |

Exit codes by category: `0` success, `1` runtime error, `2` usage error, `3` API error, `4` permission error, `5` rate-limited, `6` network unavailable.
